subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work/PB344.md LANDED. GR28 - 'If the file position indicator indicates that an optional input file is not present, the invalid key condition exists ... (See 9.1.14, Invalid key condition.)' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 PASS). The rule's own sentence was already right (status '23' per 9.1.13.5 item 3 b), the file position indicator state set only by OPEN INPUT of an absent OPTIONAL file per 14.9.27.4 GR13, the INVALID KEY transfer, execution unsuccessful). The two reasons this row was PARTIAL are both closed. (1) THE INCORPORATED 9.1.14 CONTRACT IS EDITION-INVARIANT, and that is a DETERMINATION, not an omission. 9.1.14 item 3) - 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement, any applicable exception processing statements are executed' (cite.py --check 9.1.14 PASS) - and Annex E.2 item 19 a) records that the previous standards did not run an open-mode declarative there. That reading was implemented as a <=2014 guard and WITHDRAWN: Annex E is INFORMATIVE, E.1 scopes it to 'a list of the substantive changes between the previous COBOL standard and this Working Draft International Standard' (cite.py --check E.1 PASS) - ONE prior edition, so it says nothing about 1985 or 2002 - and item 19's own justification says 'The previous COBOL Standard was not clear or missing processing of some I-O exceptions. This change clarifies or corrects that processing' (cite.py --check E.2 PASS), each sub-item adding 'This appears to be an error in previous COBOL standards'. A silence is not a prohibition, and item 19's other half is refuted outright for 1985 by that edition's own validation suite (NIST CCVS SQ122A/SQ136A/SQ137A/SQ138A/SQ148A, which the guard turned RED on CI). So 9.1.14 item 3) is served identically at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023. (2) 'No spec-derived test covers the absent-optional Format-2 leg on either organization' - pb344_use_mode_invalid_key now covers it on BOTH: C4 is the INDEXED organization (OPEN INPUT of the absent OPTIONAL file = '05', random READ with no phrase = '23', the open-mode declarative running) and C5 the RELATIVE one with the INVALID KEY phrase written (the phrase takes precedence, 14.9.49.4 GR6). C1/C2/C3 pin the unphrased-vs-phrased and mode-vs-file-name axes of the same rule. All four editions ship a copy and their four expected outputs are IDENTICAL - that identity is the edition-invariance assertion.
